neighbours.label: The 'of' (or verb) right after 'characteristic(s)' or 'qualities' meaning typical of ('is also characteristic [of] the artist', 'characteristics [of] NTM infection', 'this description [fits] Type 2 diabetes')
fire: This repetition and distancing of the main subject is also characteristic of the German artist Dieter Roth.
Pathologic changes seen on chest radiographs are characteristics of infection and suggestive of disease.
This description fits type 2 diabetes in most of the older patients we see.
Such a long delay is characteristic of the early work, which was never finished on time.
The qualities of a good teacher are patience, humour and a fair mind, and these are typical of her.
A dry, bitter finish is characteristic of this wine, which is made in the hills above the town.
Fever and a dry cough are characteristic of the illness, though not every case shows both.
Short sentences and plain words are characteristic of his later prose.
